title: Survey of human oxidoreductases and cytochrome P450 enzymes involved in the metabolism of xenobiotic and natural chemicals
funder: This work was supported in part by National Institutes of Health Grants R37 CA090426, R01 ES010546, and R01 GM103937 (to F.P.G.). The authors declare no competing financial interest.
authorConflicts: The authors declare no competing financial interest.
result: Counts of reported metabolic reactions from literature covering 1976 to 2008. Of 4192 oxidation and reduction reactions of 860 drugs, about 96% are catalysed by cytochrome P450 enzymes; flavin-containing monooxygenase, monoamine oxidase and aldo-keto reductase together account for about 5% across all chemicals. Shares of P450 reactions for drugs: CYP3A4 27%, CYP2D6 13%, CYP2C9 10%, CYP2C19 9%, CYP1A2 9%, CYP3A5 6%, CYP2C8 5%, CYP2B6 4%, CYP2E1 3%, other P450s 6%. CYP1A2, 2C9, 2C19, 2D6 and 3A4 with 3A5 account for 74%. Percentages count reported reactions, not prescriptions or clearance, and the authors call them estimates.
